newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union leader optimistic after GM meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canada union leader optimistic after GM meeting.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove emerged from a secret meeting with General Motors Corp chief executive Jack Smith, saying he was optimistic about resolving a bitter strike that has paralyzed the auto makers Canadian plants.

"I think we might have found a way to break the logjam," Hargrove told Reuters after a hastily-arranged meeting with Smith at a hotel near Toronto airport. The two talked for about hours -- the first time they have met face to face since the strike began at midnight on October 2.

Hargrove declined to elaborate, but other senior union officials predicted the two sides would soon resume negotiations to try and end the strike by 26,000 GM workers at Canadian plants. The talks have gone nowhere since last week.

High-level meetings were called off earlier today after about 160 striking workers occupied one of the carmaker's plants in Oshawa, Ontario. The workers walked off the picket lines and took over the plant after they learned GM Canada was seeking a court injunction to move some machinery from the plant to another facility to in an effort to maintain supply to customers in the United States.
Hargrove said he would attend a master committee bargaining meeting in Oshawa later today and planned to hold a news conference to discuss the outcome of his meeting with Smith.

Hargrove has accused Smith and other top GM officials of negotiating for a strike in an attempt to test the Canadian union's resolve ahead of a possible settlement with the United Autoworkers union in the United States.
The ripple effect of the Canadian strike has already idled about 10,000 U.S. and Mexican workers at plants in those countries.
